subject: Azure Marketplace: co-provisioning flow & co-sell technical checklist
messages:
From: Sara Kline <sara.kline@microsoft.com>
To: Alex Martinez <alex_martinez@redwood.ai>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-08-18T09:12:00Z
Subject: Azure marketplace co-provisioning / next steps

Hi Alex (and Vanessa),

Thanks again for the walk-through this morning. Microsoft Marketplace engineering wants to validate the co-provisioning model before we proceed to co-sell certification. High-level ask: a short technical run-through of how Redwood will provision a customer instance through the Azure listing (ARM template / Managed Identity flow), how we’ll surface telemetry for co-sell attribution, and any required telemetry hooks for Microsoft Partner Center.

Could you please: 1) confirm who from Redwood will be the technical owner for the provisioning flow, 2) share a short test plan we can run in the Microsoft sandbox, and 3) list any security evidence required (e.g., TLS cert handling, KMS/HSM usage, IP allowlists)?

We’d like to schedule a 45m working session next week with Marketplace engineering and Nimbus (the systems integrator) to walk through a dry-run. Proposed window: Tue 24 Aug or Wed 25 Aug (AM CEST). Let me know availability.

Thanks,
Sara
Sara Kline | Program Manager, Azure Marketplace Partnerships
Microsoft Corporation
From: Alex Martinez <alex_martinez@redwood.ai>
To: Sara Kline <sara.kline@microsoft.com>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>, Camila Reyes <camila_reyes@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-08-18T12:03:00Z
Subject: Re: Azure marketplace co-provisioning / next steps

Hi Sara — thanks, this is clear.

Quick answers inline: 1) Technical owner: Camila Reyes (see cc) will lead the provisioning integration; Jonas will own autoscale/testing. 2) Attached is a first-pass test plan (azure_deploy_test_plan.pdf) that covers sandbox provisioning steps, sample ARM template parameters, and end-to-end verification points (provision -> health-check -> attribution ping). 3) Security evidence: we use customer-managed keys via Azure Key Vault; for Azure Private Link scenarios we have an allowlist runbook; TLS termination is at the load balancer with mutual TLS for control-plane webhooks. I summarized required artifacts in the attached checklist (co-sell_onboarding_checklist.xlsx).

Camila — can you confirm that the ARM template we discussed supports managed identity-based provisioning and that the attribution ping includes tenant_id + subscription_id in the event payload?

Sara — Tue 24 Aug 09:30 CEST should work for us. If that’s confirmed we’ll send a calendar invite with the runbook and access details for the Microsoft sandbox subscription.

Best,
Alex
Alex Martinez | Partnerships, Redwood Inference
From: Raj Patel <raj.p@nimbuscloud.com>
To: Alex Martinez <alex_martinez@redwood.ai>, Camila Reyes <camila_reyes@redwood.ai>
Cc: Sara Kline <sara.kline@microsoft.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-08-18T16:45:00Z
Subject: Re: Azure marketplace co-provisioning / next steps

Thanks Alex — attaching a short contract redline (co-sell_contract_redline.docx) and a note on our operational constraints.

Key concerns from Nimbus ops: 
- API rate limits during bulk provisioning: we need an explicit retry/backoff strategy and a throttling window so we don't hit subscription-level throttles.
- Identity provisioning cadence: we prefer orchestration via Service Principal creation rather than long-lived keys (can Redwood support SP creation per-customer via your control plane?).
- Audit evidence: Nimbus requires a 90-day access log export for compliance audits; can Redwood provide a retention export or a pull API?

We can walk through these during the sync — our preference would be a short pre-meeting with Camila and Jonas to scope the retry/backoff tests so the sandbox run is productive.

Regards,
Raj Patel | Head of Cloud Engineering, Nimbus Cloud Consulting
From: Camila Reyes <camila_reyes@redwood.ai>
To: Raj Patel <raj.p@nimbuscloud.com>, Sara Kline <sara.kline@microsoft.com>, Alex Martinez <alex_martinez@redwood.ai>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-08-19T08:20:00Z
Subject: Re: Azure marketplace co-provisioning / next steps

Hi all — quick technical notes before the working session.

- ARM template / managed identity: yes, our template supports SystemAssigned and UserAssigned managed identities. For Nimbus's preference, we can add a Service Principal creation step in the provisioning pipeline; that flow is gated behind RBAC checks and audit logging.
- Attribution payload: we will include tenant_id, subscription_id, and marketplace_purchase_id in the attribution event. Events are emitted to an internal telemetry topic and forwarded to Microsoft’s Partner Center endpoint over TLS with client certs.
- Rate limiting: Jonas (cc) will own the throttling tests. Our control plane has a configurable queue with exponential backoff and a per-subscription concurrency cap; we will provide observability during the sandbox test so Nimbus can validate.

Jonas — can you run a short smoke test against the sandbox with 50 concurrent provisioning requests and capture the retry metrics? I’ll share the minimal test harness tomorrow.

Camila
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
From: Sara Kline <sara.kline@microsoft.com>
